data.title: Shackelford, McKinley & Norton Strengthens Expertise in Dallas Office
data.description:
Shackelford, McKinley & Norton Strengthens Expertise in Dallas Office

Firm adds to industry-leading aviation, commercial litigation, real estate practices

Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP, announces the addition of partners Chris Andrews, J Bailey and Joe Marcus to its aviation and commercial litigation practices. Also joining the firm is real estate associate Nithin Shakamuri. All join the noted full-service transactional and litigation firm’s Dallas office.

Mr. Andrews joins the firm’s internationally recognized aviation practice with a background in regulatory compliance and aircraft leasing and procurement. He is a former attorney with the Federal Aviation Administration’s Office of the Chief Counsel, where he specialized in advising FAA clients on safety reporting programs and safety management systems. He also was FAA counsel for claims arising from the Tort Claims Act.

A member of the Aviation Lawyers Association, Mr. Andrews is a graduate of Drake University College of Law and holds an LL.M. in international aviation law and policy from the DePaul University College of Law.

Mr. Bailey represents owners, contractors, subcontractors and developers across the life of their residential and commercial construction projects. He has served as first-chair counsel in arbitrations, bench and jury trials, leading trial teams from jury selection through closing arguments.

The University of Oklahoma School of Law graduate also frequently serves in an outside general counsel role for clients, negotiating and drafting construction contracts, assisting with employment matters and advising on business issues.

Mr. Marcus is a litigator with more than a decade of experience representing businesses, including electric utilities and cooperatives, in complex, high-exposure litigation involving commercial and contract disputes, defense of catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death claims, construction and real estate disputes, multi-party lawsuits, easement negotiation and easement disputes.

A graduate of the University of Miami School of Law, Mr. Marcus is admitted to practice in Texas, Florida and Colorado. He is a member of the Electric Cooperative Bar Association.

Mr. Shakamuri works with property owners, developers, investors and businesses across a variety of industries, focusing on commercial real estate, corporate and business matters involving real estate acquisitions and dispositions, commercial leasing, development, financing, and mergers and acquisitions.

He is the co-chair of the Dallas Association of Young Lawyers’ transactional law committee and was a member of its 2025 Leadership Class. He is a Brown Family Philanthropy Fellow with Social Venture Partners Dallas. He earned his J.D. from the University of Oklahoma College of Law and an LL.M. in taxation from the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law.

About Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP

Shackelford, McKinley & Norton, LLP, is a full-service transactional, litigation, aviation and entertainment law firm with attorneys and offices in Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth and Austin, Texas, and New Orleans.

Hundreds of Clinicians Share PROTEIN NOW!™ Protein Shots

PROTEIN NOW!™ earns Clinicians' Choice status on FrontrowMD, where more than 800 clinicians and counting have shared the zero sugar, 21 gram protein shot out of hundreds of product options. No clinicians were compensated.

More than 800 clinicians, including physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician associates, have added PROTEIN NOW! to their personalized FrontrowMD patient pages as of November 2026, and that number continues to grow.

Clinicians use FrontrowMD, a free platform, to build their own selection of health products, and FrontrowMD digitally tracks and verifies which products they include. Products shared by clinicians on FrontrowMD are recognized with its Clinicians' Choice designation.

"Getting your protein in should be easy, and it should come from a product you can feel good about," said Alex Berrio, Director of Marketing at NutraBio Labs. "Seeing hundreds of clinicians share PROTEIN NOW! gives people one more reason to grab one and go."

PROTEIN NOW! is made for people who know protein matters but struggle to fit it into busy days: commuters, parents, travelers, and the growing number of people on GLP-1 medications looking for protein in smaller, easier-to-consume servings. Each 3.38 fl oz shot delivers 21 grams of protein in just 90 calories and requires no mixing, refrigeration, or preparation.

Dr. Salvador Recio, MD, an internal medicine physician with 35 years in practice, wrote: "A lot of protein drinks come with sugar and calories that people don't want, which is why this protein shot from Protein Now! gets my attention." He added: "Notably, it contains no sugar, no fat, and barely any carbohydrates."

Dr. Katie Novitski, MD, a surgeon with 11 years in practice, wrote: "Protein Now! packs a full serving of protein into a small bottle, so the whole thing goes down in a couple of swallows." She added: "Because it is such a concentrated protein source, a good amount can fit into a very small drink."

†These clinician want to clarify that larger-scale research to support their product claims is still developing. These statements have not been reviewed by the FDA and are not intended to be medical advice.

PROTEIN NOW! is available in Orange Mango, Strawberry Watermelon, and Blueberry Acai at proteinnow.com, nutrabio.com, Amazon, and select specialty retailers. Visit our website to learn more and see the clinicians sharing PROTEIN NOW! protein shots.

data.title: 'I've been a stay-at-home mom': I'm 50 and have a chronic illness. My husband lost his job. Should he raid his 401(k)?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning'

"COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage financially." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I am 50, and my husband recently lost his job. I have been a stay-at-home mom for many years and also live with a chronic illness that limits my ability to work full-time. I recently started working as a daycare aide at our local public school, but our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning.

I have several questions:

1. Health insurance and access to medical care

Unfortunately, my husband was not transparent with me about the circumstances surrounding his employment, so I wasn't given the opportunity to plan ahead for my healthcare needs. My health insurance was tied to his employment and, as a result, I was unable to renew my specialty medications or schedule an appointment with my neurologist.

COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage. What other options should I explore? Are there affordable health insurance alternatives, marketplace plans, or assistance programs that could help someone in my situation?

2. My husband's 401(k) and retirement savings

My husband is considering withdrawing money from his 401(k). These funds are intended to support us during retirement. What is the best way to handle his 401(k)? Would rolling it over into an IRA or another retirement account be a better option than withdrawing the money? Are there ways to transfer or invest these funds without triggering unnecessary taxes?

3. My personal savings and retirement planning

I have $150,000 in a money-market account earning 3.1% interest. This money represents savings from my previous employment, along with funds I consistently set aside from our monthly household budget over the years. I want to make sure I am being responsible with this money and putting it to work for my future.

What would be the best way to manage these savings for retirement? Should I keep the money in a money-market account, consider CDs or high-yield savings accounts, or explore other investment options that could provide better long-term growth while protecting my principal? I need to make informed decisions and protect my financial future.

Feeling Insecure

Related: 'I have no financial safety net': I'm 66, rely on Social Security and have just $500 in savings. What hope do I have?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually. Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group.

He can apply for insurance outside the normal open-enrollment period from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace.

Dear Insecure,

Your healthcare plan is an immediate priority, so sort that out ASAP.

Losing workplace health insurance qualifies your husband for a special enrollment period on healthcare.gov. He has a 60-day window after the loss of his coverage to pick a plan. The ACA Marketplace may ask for documents, including an employer or insurer notice, to verify when his coverage ends. The ACA Marketplace calculates his premium based on his age, location, household size and expected household income for the entire calendar year.

Importantly, he can apply outside the normal open-enrollment period, which runs from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace. He may also qualify for an ACA subsidy. If he was earning $45,000 before being laid off and, assuming he doesn't have another job to go to, he will earn less for the remainder of the year; he will need to estimate his total income for 2026, which includes his salary up until the time he was laid off and unemployment benefits.

There is no asset test for most adults under 65 who qualify for the ACA Marketplace through the rules based on their modified adjusted gross income (MAGI). MAGI is calculated using adjusted gross income, taking certain adjustments or deductions into account. It's used to determine eligibility for certain tax deductions and credits, as well as certain government benefits and surcharges. The formula can change depending on what benefits you are applying for.

It's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

If your husband applies through the ACA Marketplace and his income appears low enough for Medicaid rather than Marketplace subsidies, the application should probably be referred to the relevant state program. Given that he has just lost his job and his income has dropped, tell him to check both state healthcare plans and ACA Marketplace plans. As you point out, it's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

COBRA can cost $800 a month for individual coverage and $2,300 for family coverage, depending on the plan. Again, he has 60 days to elect COBRA, and once he pays the required premiums, his coverage can be applied retroactively to when his employer coverage ended. To qualify for COBRA, the U.S. Labor Department says he must have been covered by his employer's group health plan, the plan must be subject to COBRA, and other qualifying conditions must be met.

Some Moneyist Facebook Group members weighed in on your questions. "Don't get distracted with things that don't matter," one wrote. "Rolling over your husband's 401(k) is not a priority. It can stay in his employer's custodian and roll over to a Schwab or Fidelity-type institution when things calm down. His focus needs to be 100% on getting a new job, not worrying about your retirement. You are nowhere near ready for retirement so employment is what matters."

Don't miss: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

Retirement savings and planning

I understand why you and your husband might think withdrawing from your 401(k) could help, but it could have the opposite effect in the long run. I urge you to proceed cautiously. There's increasing evidence that, with the rising cost of living and stubbornly high interest rates, more Americans feel under pressure to dip into their retirement savings - sometimes as a short-term loan, which they may not be able to pay back.

If your husband does dip into his 401(k), he may be forced to pay a 10% penalty for withdrawing funds before 591/2 and, if that wasn't harsh enough, he will also be required to pay income tax on his early withdrawal. For example, if you need $50,000 to supplement your living expenses over the next 12 months, he may need to withdraw considerably more to account for taxes and potential penalties. The IRS has effectively made every effort to deter you from doing so.

There is a "rule of 55" for making unexpected or early withdrawals. If a person leaves or loses their job during or after the calendar year they turn 55, or age 50 for certain public-safety workers, they can make withdrawals from a 401(k) plan without having to pay that 10% penalty. Income taxes still apply, however, and the funds must remain in that employer's 401(k) rather than being rolled over to an IRA.

We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment.

Given your age, investing your $150,000 in a diversified stock-market portfolio could make more sense than a money-market account, high-yield savings account (HYSA) or CD. Keeping it in a money-market account (at a 3.1% interest rate) could give you around $203,500 over 10 years versus $222,000 in a HYSA or CD (at 4%), or $295,000 in a balanced portfolio (at 7%). The big caveat is that the stock market provides no guarantees.

There are no hard-and-fast rules, but many advisers recommend that someone around 50 consider an asset allocation of 60% to 80% equities and 20% to 40% fixed income (bonds and cash equivalents). However, your risk tolerance plays a big part in that. It would not be unusual to find someone who is invested in 90% or even, in some cases, 100% stocks at 50, given that they have another 15 years or more until they retire.

In the meantime, cut your costs and look into selling any valuables that could get you through this financial crunch. I trust your husband has applied for unemployment insurance and has pursued your health-insurance options before that 60-day window has closed. You will need patience. We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment. The average job search takes about three to six months, so be prepared for a hard slog.

Keep your cool and don't make any hasty decisions.

Related: My 93-year-old father changed his will at the 11th hour, leaving my brother his entire $500,000 estate. Can I challenge it?

More columns from Quentin Fottrell:

'Just watch Judge Judy': I'm in my 70s. Why do people keep making the same avoidable financial mistakes?

'She wants him gone': My friend took in a homeless man as a caretaker. After 10 years, how can she evict him?

'Our family is broken beyond repair': My brother took over my parents' finances. What can I do?

By emailing your questions to The Moneyist or posting your dilemmas on The Moneyist Facebook group, you agree to have them published anonymously on MarketWatch.

-Quentin Fottrell

data.title: Pexar Wins CES Innovation Awards® 2027 Honor for PexarBolt Ultra TBT5 Dock with Visual Dashboard
data.description:
Pexar Wins CES Innovation Awards® 2027 Honor for PexarBolt Ultra TBT5 Dock with Visual Dashboard

Pexar Wins CES Innovation Awards® 2027 Honor for PexarBolt Ultra TBT5 Dock with Visual Dashboard

PR Newswire

HONG KONG, Nov. 20, 2026

HONG KONG, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pexar, a smart device brand powered by Lexar, announced that the PexarBolt Ultra TBT5 Dock has been selected as a CES Innovation Awards® 2027 Honoree in the Computer Peripherals & Accessories category. This new honor comes just two months after PexarBolt Ultra's initial launch at IFA 2026, where it was named a 2026 IFA Innovation Awards Honoree in the Content Creation Technology category.

PexarBolt Ultra's Kickstarter campaign has drawn more than US$740,000 from over 1,300 backers, including Late Pledges. That total is 70-plus times its funding goal.

Since its debut, the PexarBolt Ultra has been covered by outlets including PCWorld, TechRadar, PetaPixel, Cult of Mac and Notebookcheck.

As the world's first Thunderbolt 5 dock to feature a 5-inch touch control dashboard in a compact aluminum design, the PexarBolt Ultra shows the performance and status of connected devices in real time. Complementing the touchscreen is a precision metal dial that provides a tactile control option. And with AI Status, users can approve or reject requests from supported AI coding agents directly from the dock.

Two features unlocked during the Kickstarter campaign take the dashboard further. With PexarBolt Plugins, users can use the AI tools they already know to create their own plugins for the dock's touchscreen, from a KVM switcher that moves displays and USB devices between two computers, to one-tap controls for apps like Photoshop and music, to live status boards for coding projects. Plugin Studio offers free, open-source examples to start from, and users can share what they create with the PexarBolt community. 60W AVS fast charging adds quicker charging for compatible smartphones.

Featuring up to 80 Gbps of bidirectional bandwidth, and up to 120 Gbps for display-heavy work with Thunderbolt 5 Bandwidth Boost, the PexarBolt Ultra delivers fast performance for large file transfers and multi-display workflows. A single Thunderbolt 5 cable connects to all of its 22 ports, including USB-C, 10GbE Ethernet, CFexpress Type B and SD card readers, and DisplayPort 2.1, plus an integrated PCIe Gen 4 M.2 SSD slot. The dock also delivers up to 140W of charging to a connected laptop. In extended workloads, smart active cooling and the metal design dissipate heat to increase reliability and stability.

Availability

The PexarBolt Ultra TBT5 Dock's Kickstarter campaign closed on Nov. 7, 2026, and Late Pledges are now open. Backers who missed the campaign can still reserve the dock through Late Pledge for US$499. The official retail price is US$649.

The PexarBolt Ultra will also be on display at CES 2027 in Las Vegas, Jan. 6-9, at the Lexar booth (#24138, Central Hall, Las Vegas Convention Center).

Full product information is available on Pexar's website.
Late Pledges are open on Kickstarter.
Explore and share plugins in the PexarBolt Plugin Community.

About Pexar

Powered by Lexar, Pexar crafts premium products for life-sharing and creative workflows, from digital displays to precision desktop accessories. For more information, please visit pexar.com, or find Pexar on Instagram, Facebook and YouTube.

Contact
marketing@pexar.com 

The CES Innovation Awards are based upon descriptive materials submitted to the judges. CTA did not verify the accuracy of any submission or of any claims made and did not test the item to which the award was given.

data.description:
Lost Money on Alibaba Group Holding Limited Shares? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Investigates Potential Securities Fraud After 7.05% Stock Decline

Investigation centers on the November 12, 2026 news about Alibaba Group Holding Limited; investors with losses may have potential claims to recover them

Alibaba Group Holding Limited ("Alibaba" or the "Company") investors who lost money may have claims to recover their losses. The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz today announced it is investigating potential securities fraud claims on behalf of investors in Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA), examining whether the Company may have violated the federal securities laws. The investigation centers on the disclosure about Alibaba Group Holding Limited on November 12, 2026.

If you lost money on Alibaba Group Holding Limited securities, share your Alibaba Group Holding Limited loss information with the firm to learn about potentially pursuing a claim to recover your losses.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited investigation at a glance

  • Date of disclosure: November 12, 2026
  • Share price decline: $7.16 per share, or 7.05%
  • Closing price: $94.36 on November 12, 2026

What happened?

On November 9, 2026, the Financial Times published an article alleging “[t]he woman at the center of the Nvidia spying scandal pitched an AI chips deal to China-based investors, touting her ability to secure the US company's coveted GPUs and her commercial relationship with Chinese tech giant Alibaba.” The article further stated “Alibaba was Megaspeed's anchor customer” and “Nvidia first met Megaspeed to discuss potential procurement because the company had shown their leasing contract with Alibaba.”

On this news, Alibaba stock fell $4.07, or 3.71%, to close at $105.38 on November 9, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Then, on November 12, 2026, before the market opened, Reuters published an article entitled "Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of US curbs". The article stated “Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China, worried that the scandal involving the US chipmaker's CEO Jensen Huang could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors”.

On this news, Alibaba stock fell $7.16, or 7.05%, to close at $94.36 on November 12, 2026, thereby further injuring investors.

"Alibaba Group Holding Limited shares dropped 7.05% after it was disclosed on November 12, 2026 that Reuters reported that Chinese AI firms were rushing to rent Nvidia chip capacity abroad, fearing tighter US curbs. Our investigation will look at whether investors had complete and accurate information before that disclosure," said Frank R. Cruz of The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz.

What should Alibaba Group Holding Limited investors do now?

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is investigating potential claims on behalf of Alibaba Group Holding Limited investors. Investors who lost money can visit the Alibaba Group Holding Limited investigation page, email info@frankcruzlaw.com, or call 310-914-5007.

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

Questions and answers about the Alibaba Group Holding Limited investigation

Who is eligible? Investors who purchased Alibaba Group Holding Limited securities and suffered losses may have claims, and can contact the firm to find out whether the Alibaba Group Holding Limited investigation affects them.

What does a securities fraud investigation involve? In the Alibaba Group Holding Limited investigation, The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is examining whether the Company or its executives may have made false or misleading statements to investors in violation of the federal securities laws.

Is there a lawsuit? This release announces an investigation by The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz, not a lawsuit. If a securities class action is later filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, investors may be able to seek appointment as lead plaintiff.

How are attorneys' fees handled? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz works on contingency, so Alibaba Group Holding Limited investors pay no attorneys' fees up front. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses come only from a recovery, if there is one, and require court approval.

Information for whistleblowers

Anyone with non-public information about Alibaba Group Holding Limited should consider their options to assist the investigation or participate in the SEC Whistleblower Program. The program allows whistleblowers who provide original information leading to a successful SEC enforcement action to receive awards of 10 to 30 percent of the sanctions collected, when those sanctions exceed $1 million. For more information, contact Frank R. Cruz at 310-914-5007 or email info@frankcruzlaw.com.

About The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz investigates and prosecutes securities fraud and corporate malfeasance class actions. With nearly 20 years of litigation experience, the firm focuses on complex securities class actions and gives each client personal, one-on-one attention throughout the legal process.

Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

data.title: Enmarket to Open Newest Eatery Location in Rincon, GA

WORCESTER, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Nouria, a family-owned convenience, food, and fuel retailer serving New England and the Southeast, will hold the Grand Opening of its newest Eatery location in its Rincon, GA Enmarket store at 6188 Highway 21 South, on Monday, November 23rd. The Eatery is Enmarket's proprietary fresh food concept inside select Enmarket convenience stores.

The Eatery is known for fresh prepared foods, especially Southern comfort-food like fried chicken and specialty hot side dishes. In addition, the Eatery offers fresh-cracked-egg breakfast sandwiches, hearty subs, savory pizza, and other delicious options prepared with convenience and quality in mind. Guests will be able to sample several of these items on the 23rd. Special Grand Opening offers include two slices of pepperoni or cheese pizza and a large fountain drink for $4, and a chicken sandwich, potato wedges, and large fountain drink for $4.99. Both specials are available through December 20th.

"We are excited to bring The Eatery to our Rincon location so guests can enjoy our delicious fresh food and have another reason to visit us here," said Joy Almekies, director of fresh food and culinary at Nouria. "We want our guests to think of Enmarket when it comes to delicious, fresh food in addition to being convenient place to stop for on-the-go items."

About Nouria

Nouria is a family-owned convenience, food, and fuel retail company headquartered in Worcester, Massachusetts. Founded in 1989 by Tony El-Nemr, the company operates more than 300 convenience store locations, 93 car washes, and multiple travel centers across New England and the Southeast. Nouria also supplies fuel to independent retail sites under brands including Shell, Irving, Gulf, Sunoco, and Citgo. The company is committed to delivering an outstanding guest experience and supporting the communities it serves.

data.title: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Wisconsin Republican Sen. Ron Johnson called Social Security a 'scam' and urged lawmakers to shut it down

Social Security is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi scheme is born of fraud and relies on a constant stream of new unwitting investors.

Fear can lead us to do and say unexpected things.

It can push us toward panic selling, drive us to make wild assumptions about the world, and sometimes force us to take a hard look at our own finances. We are especially prone to these impulses when we are looking for something or someone to blame.

Wisconsin Republican Sen. Ron Johnson, the chairman of the Committee on the Budget, on Wednesday took aim at Social Security ahead of a hearing on the subject, calling it a scam. "It's grotesque and at this point, there really is no way to fix Social Security," he said. "It is a Ponzi scheme."

Social Security is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi scheme is born of fraud and relies on a stream of new unwitting investors who pay the returns promised to earlier ones. Social Security is a pay-as-you-go program established by federal law, in which payroll taxes fund benefits.

He isn't the only one who's frustrated with Social Security. Experts attribute an expected shortfall in Social Security to demographic factors - older workers retiring, with some claiming benefits early out of fear that the funds will run out.

Social Security is a pay-as-you-go program established by federal law.

Unless Congress acts, the combined trust funds will run out in 2034, covering just 83% of benefits. A new AARP report said: "The share of gross domestic product subject to Social Security's payroll tax, the program's primary income source, has fallen steadily over the past four decades."

The Social Security taxable maximum is $184,500 for 2026 and $192,300 for 2027, meaning earnings above those limits are not subject to Social Security payroll taxes. In other words, a growing share of national income is excluded, contributing to the expected shortfall in funds.

Like Johnson, a Moneyist reader also used the "P" word. "The thought of living to 100 terrifies me more than dying. For me, the biggest fraud is telling people to wait until 70 to retire just to maximize their Social Security benefits - as if that's the only factor worth considering."

They continued: "I grew up in the 1980s, and the advice to never count on Social Security is sounding more and more like a warning than a prediction. I fear there will be a run on Social Security similar to the bank runs before the Great Depression. Long live the Ponzi!"

Don't miss: Is $1 million enough for a household to retire? The answer keeps changing.

Addressing the criticisms

The reader is essentially asking four questions: (1) Will fear trigger a Social Security crisis? (2) Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? (3) Why sacrifice your 60s to get a bigger check at 70? And (4) Can you really count on Social Security?

(1) As for fear leading to a crisis: Probably not, so do not get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom and gloom. A run on a bank involves a large number of people withdrawing their money and, if the bank cannot meet those withdrawals, even an otherwise solvent institution can fail.

I grew up in the 1980s too, and here's a fun fact about Generation X: The American Institute of Stress says we are apparently more stressed out than other generations. The main reason for that, researchers theorize, is that we are worried about falling short on our retirement goals.

(2) Social Security is a social-insurance program funded by workers and employers to provide support in retirement, prevent vulnerable people from falling into poverty and provide economic stability during downturns. It is at risk of a shortfall in funding, not annihilation.

Social Security is at risk of a shortfall in funding, not annihilation.

(3) You can claim Social Security at 62, but doing so reduces your monthly benefit by 30% compared with waiting until your full retirement age (FRA) of 67. Waiting until 70 increases your benefit by 8% for each year you delay beyond 67. That's 24% more in total.

If you are collecting Social Security and remain below FRA throughout 2026, you can earn up to $24,480 before benefits are withheld. Above that limit, $1 is withheld for every $2 you earn. At FRA, Social Security recalculates your benefit to account for withholdings.

Yes, some people do claim Social Security benefits early due to fears about the program's long-term viability. But the program values stability, security and peace of mind over recklessness, madcap investments and promises of riches.

(4) You can count on Social Security, which is not projected to disappear. Payroll taxes and other incoming revenue will keep funding benefits. Under current projections, though, that revenue would cover only 83% of scheduled benefits from the combined trust funds in 2034.

Don't miss: 'I still have horrible memories of the Bernie Madoff scandal': At 63, who can I trust with my $655K retirement fund?

Why we have Social Security

Social Security was created in 1935 in response to the Great Depression and was not intended to maximize investment returns. Today, it provides a social safety net against the financial hardships of retirement, disability and the loss of a family's breadwinner.

There are two separate funds: the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund and the Disability Insurance Trust Fund. Their reserves are invested in special-issue U.S. Treasury securities, backed by the full faith and credit of the federal government.

So what about this looming funding crisis? The Congressional Budget Office said earlier this year that the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, which pays retirement and survivors benefits, is projected to run out of reserves in 2032.

The Bipartisan Policy Center, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, said in a June report that, at that point, incoming revenue would cover just 78% of scheduled benefits from that fund. Without congressional action, those shortfalls would mean across-the-board reductions in benefits.

There is already a demographic 'run' on Social Security.

"The program's long-run outlook worsened significantly this year," it said. "The Social Security Administration (SSA) revised its fertility and immigration projections downward." The 75-year shortfall has risen to approximately $30 trillion - up from $26 trillion last year.

There is already a demographic "run" on Social Security. The Bipartisan Policy Center said "an aging population is a major contributor to the problem." The ratio of workers to beneficiaries has dropped from 5-to-1 in 1960 to 2.6-to-1 in 2025 and is projected to fall to 1.9-to-1 by 2075.

The Social Security Disability Insurance Trust Fund is projected to remain solvent until 2100, the end of the Board of Trustees' 75-year projection period, but the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, under current estimates, won't have enough to pay full benefits in 2032.

We are encouraged to delay our dream life, save more, work longer and maximize our retirement contributions. Still, the price of financial security should not be spending our 60s worrying about our 70s, 80s and 90s, and beyond. For millions of people, however, that worry is a daily reality.

Keep calm and carry on working, if you can, and saving for retirement.

Related: Should wealthier Americans forgo their Social Security benefits as a charitable gesture?
